title: The moment relief came, they broke their word.
subtitle: A reprieve for a set term, and a broken promise

row.title: a set term
sub: time given to keep my word

then: Each time Musa prayed, Allah lifted the affliction for a fixed term. And each time, as Sa'id bin Jubayr describes, {trap}they did not believe and did not let the Children of Israel go{/trap}. Ibn Ishaq says this happened after the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood.
now: After the panic attack you swear you will stop working till 2am. The next week feels fine, and the laptop is open at midnight again. {idea}The relief was not the end of the story. It was the time given to keep the promise.{/idea}
old: Once the danger passes, I can go back to normal.
new: Relief is a deadline to keep my word, not a release from it.
try: Think of the last time Allah lifted a worry for you. Do one thing today that honors what you promised then.

title: Many warnings ignored, and then the sea closed.
subtitle: The end of Fir'awn and his army
then: After all the signs, Fir'awn and his soldiers chased Musa into the sea that Allah had parted. Ibn Kathir says that {trap}when they had all entered, the sea closed over them{/trap}. The verse gives the reason: they denied Allah's signs and were heedless of them.
now: Heedlessness is quiet. It is the reminder you swipe away, the Friday you skip, the warning in your own chest you talk over. {idea}No single moment feels like a choice.{/idea} The verse asks you to notice while the sea is still open.
old: Ignoring a few reminders is not a big deal.
new: Heedlessness, repeated, is what closes the door.
try: Today, when a reminder of Allah crosses your day, stop for ten seconds instead of moving past it.

title: The oppressed inherited the land because they endured.
subtitle: Patience fulfilled a promise; pride lost its buildings
then: Allah gave the people who were considered weak the blessed land, which Al-Hasan and Qatadah said was Sham. {reward}The good word of your Lord was fulfilled because of their endurance.{/reward} Ibn Kathir links this to 28:5-6. And all that Fir'awn built and grew was destroyed.
now: You are the junior at work who does honest work while others take shortcuts and get noticed. You stay patient for years. {reward}Patience is not doing nothing.{/reward} It is holding steady while Allah's promise ripens.
old: The strong always win in the end.
new: Allah's promise is fulfilled for those who endure, and pride's buildings do not last.
try: Name one situation where you are holding on patiently. Ask Allah today to accept your sabr.

title: Just saved by a miracle, they asked for an idol.
subtitle: Wanting what the neighbors have, right after the sea

row.title: be like them
sub: they have one, so should we

then: Having just crossed the sea, the Children of Israel passed a people devoted to idols, which Ibn Jarir said were shaped like cows. They asked Musa for a god like theirs. Ibn Kathir cites a hadith: on the way to Hunayn, some new Muslims asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sacred tree like the pagans had. He said: {trap}you said just what the people of Musa said{/trap}.
now: Your friends all have a lucky charm, a horoscope app, a thing they touch before an exam. You start to want one too, just in case. {idea}The pull to copy what others hold sacred is old and strong.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me has it, it cannot be that bad.
new: Copying others' devotion right after Allah has saved me is forgetting who saved me.
try: Notice one habit you picked up only because others do it. Ask if it pulls you toward Allah or away.

title: What they worship will perish, and their work is in vain.
subtitle: Musa explains why the idols are worth nothing
then: Musa told his people that the idol worshippers they admired {trap}would perish in what they were doing{/trap}, and that all their work was in vain. Ibn Kathir says Musa was correcting their ignorance of Allah's greatness and His purity from any partner.
now: You see people giving their whole lives to a career, a team, an image. They are so devoted it looks admirable. {idea}Devotion is only as valuable as what it is aimed at.{/idea}
old: Anyone that devoted must be onto something.
new: Devotion aimed at anything other than Allah ends in nothing.
try: Look at where most of your energy went this week. Redirect ten minutes of it to Allah today.

title: Shall I seek a god other than Allah, who honored you?
subtitle: Musa reminds them what Allah already gave
then: Musa asked them: shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, when He has given you superiority over the nations? Ibn Kathir says he {reward}reminded them of Allah's blessings{/reward}, saving them from Fir'awn's tyranny and humiliation.
now: You have a home, health, a family that calls. Then a new phone comes out and you feel empty without it. {reward}Remembering what Allah has already given{/reward} makes the craving much smaller.
old: Something is missing, so I need something new.
new: When I remember what Allah gave me, I stop looking elsewhere to fill the gap.
try: List five things Allah has given you that you did not earn. Read the list once tonight.

title: Remember the worst days He brought you out of.
subtitle: Rescue from Fir'awn, and the trial within it
then: Allah reminds the Children of Israel how He saved them from Fir'awn's people, who {trap}killed their sons and kept their women alive{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says Musa reminded them of this to show what Allah had done, and the verse calls it {idea}a great trial from your Lord{/idea}.
now: You forget the year you could not pay rent, the night in the emergency room, the season of feeling completely alone. Life is easier now and you grumble about small things. {reward}Remembering the rescue{/reward} puts today in its place.
old: The hard years are behind me, better not to think about them.
new: Remembering where Allah brought me from keeps me grateful and humble.
try: Think of one hard time Allah brought you through. Say alhamdulillah for it specifically.

title: Forty nights alone with his Lord, and a trust left behind.
subtitle: Musa's appointment, and Harun left in charge
then: Allah appointed thirty nights for Musa and added ten. Ibn Kathir says scholars mention {idea}Musa fasted this period{/idea}, before receiving the Tawrah. He left his brother Harun with the people and told him to act rightly. Ibn Kathir notes this was only a reminder, since Harun was a noble prophet himself.
now: You hand your team to a colleague while you go on leave. Or you leave the kids with your sibling for a weekend. {idea}A short, clear reminder of what matters{/idea} is not distrust. It is care.
old: Reminding someone good feels like I do not trust them.
new: Even the best people benefit from a gentle reminder to do right.
try: Before handing something over this week, give one short reminder of what matters most, kindly.

title: The mountain could not bear it, and Musa fell.
subtitle: Longing to see Allah, and learning one's limits
then: Allah spoke to Musa directly, and Musa asked to see Him. Allah said he could not, and to look at the mountain. When Allah manifested to it, it collapsed to dust and Musa fell unconscious. Ibn Kathir notes that {reward}believers will see Allah in the Hereafter{/reward}, citing 75:22-23. Musa woke saying {idea}Glory be to You, I turn to You{/idea}.
now: Sometimes your heart wants more than this life can hold: certainty, closeness, answers. The longing is not wrong. {idea}Musa's answer was praise and turning back{/idea}, trusting that what is not given here is kept for later.
old: If I cannot have it now, it must not be meant for me.
new: Some things are too great for this world, and Allah keeps them for the next.
try: When you feel a longing you cannot satisfy, say subhanak and make dua for Jannah.

title: Take what I gave you, and be among the grateful.
subtitle: Chosen with a message, told to hold it and thank
then: Right after Musa asked to see Allah, he was told he had been chosen by Allah's messages and speech. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}hold to what I have given you and be grateful{/idea}, and do not ask for what is beyond your capacity to bear.
now: You keep thinking about the house you do not have, the talent you wish you had. Meanwhile you have a Quran on your phone, two hands, a quiet hour each morning. {reward}Take what you were given, and thank Him for it.{/reward}
old: I will be grateful when I get what I am hoping for.
new: Gratitude starts with holding firmly to what I already have.
try: Pick one gift you already have. Use it well today, and thank Allah for it out loud.

title: Hold it with strength, and take the best of it.
subtitle: The Tablets, given to be lived firmly
then: Allah wrote for Musa on the Tablets exhortation and explanation for all things. Ibn Kathir explains {idea}hold unto these with firmness{/idea} as being firm in obedience. He was to tell his people to take the best of it, and was warned he would see the home of the rebellious.
now: You read an ayah that moves you on Friday. By Monday it is gone, lost between emails and errands. {idea}Taking it with strength{/idea} means picking one thing from it and holding it all week.
old: I read it, so I have taken it.
new: Guidance is meant to be held with strength, not glanced at.
try: Choose one line of the Quran today. Write it somewhere you will see it every day this week.

title: Arrogance blinds a person to every sign.
subtitle: Seeing the right path and choosing the wrong one

row.title: lack of proof
sub: what I think the problem is

then: Allah says He will turn away from His signs those who are arrogant without right. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}just as they acted proudly without justification, Allah let them be disgraced with ignorance{/trap}. Sufyan bin 'Uyaynah said it means losing understanding of the Quran, and Ibn Kathir notes this applies in every nation.
now: Your spouse is right about something and you know it. But admitting it feels like losing, so you double down. {trap}Pride makes the wrong path look easier than the right one.{/trap} The more you do it, the harder it is to see.
old: I would change if someone showed me I was wrong.
new: Arrogance makes me blind to the very signs that would guide me.
try: Today, say I was wrong about one small thing to someone who deserves to hear it.

title: Deeds without faith in the meeting come to nothing.
subtitle: Each person is repaid for what they did

row.title: what I do
sub: good for good, evil for evil

then: Those who deny Allah's signs and the meeting in the Hereafter find their deeds made void. Ibn Kathir explains it as recompense matching action: {idea}good for good and evil for evil. As you sow, you reap.{/idea}
now: You plant tomatoes in the spring and you get tomatoes in summer, not roses. Every word to your kids, every hour at work, every choice in private is a seed. {reward}The harvest will match what you planted.{/reward}
old: What happens in the end is out of my hands.
new: I will be repaid for exactly what I did, so I can plant better today.
try: Do one good deed today with the meeting with Allah in mind, quietly, for Him alone.
